general_rules: Classify each field from the supplied title/abstract text only. Naming a model or mechanism that matches a code's definition is stated evidence for that code: this is classification by definition, not inference.
Assign several codes when the work explicitly studies several (e.g. two model families compared).
Use not_reported only when the text gives no basis for any code of that field.
Use other_* codes only for identifiable items outside the listed codes, never for items the listed definitions cover.
Evidence is a verbatim excerpt from one supplied source that supports the chosen code(s).
Add an other_* code alongside a listed code only when the text explicitly reports a distinct item that no listed code covers; never add other_* for aspects already captured by a listed code.

A named canonical model entails its standard representation and mechanism: bounded-confidence models entail continuous opinions and bounded_assimilation; linear-averaging models (DeGroot, Friedkin-Johnsen) entail continuous opinions and assimilation; voter-family models (voter, majority rule, Sznajd, q-voter) entail discrete opinions and assimilation; Axelrod entails other_representation (trait vectors). Code these unless the text states otherwise.

model_family.bounded_confidence: Agents are influenced only by opinions within a confidence threshold: Deffuant-Weisbuch, Hegselmann-Krause, relative agreement, and bounded-confidence variants (noise, heterogeneous thresholds, repulsion added).
model_family.linear_averaging: Weighted averaging of others' opinions without a threshold: DeGroot, French-Harary, Friedkin-Johnsen (stubbornness/anchoring), Abelson, Taylor, linear consensus protocols applied to opinions.
model_family.voter: Discrete-state copying or local-majority updating: voter model and variants (noisy, nonlinear, q-voter), Galam majority rule, Sznajd, invasion and link-update processes.
model_family.other_named_family: An identifiable model outside the three families above: Axelrod cultural dissemination, social impact/Ising-type, Bayesian or naive social learning, argument-communication, CODA, contagion/epidemic models applied to opinions, game-theoretic opinion formation, LLM-agent opinion simulations.
model_family.not_reported: No model family identifiable from the text.

influence_mechanism.assimilation: Opinions move toward others' opinions (averaging, copying, persuasion toward the source) without a similarity restriction.
influence_mechanism.bounded_assimilation: Assimilation restricted to sufficiently similar others (confidence threshold or similarity-gated influence).
influence_mechanism.social_learning: Beliefs updated by inference from others' signals, choices or actions (Bayesian or heuristic learning).
influence_mechanism.repulsion: Opinions move away from dissimilar or disliked others: negative influence, anticonformity, backfire, rejection.
influence_mechanism.other_mechanism: Only an explicitly named mechanism outside the listed codes: reinforcement, argument exchange, media or algorithmic exposure effects, external fields, stubbornness-only dynamics.

opinion_representation.continuous: Real-valued opinions on an interval or real line.
opinion_representation.discrete: Binary or finite categorical opinion states.
opinion_representation.other_representation: Multidimensional vectors, cultural trait vectors, belief networks, argument sets, probability distributions or other structured states.

network_topology.spatial: Lattices, grids or spatially embedded interaction.
network_topology.synthetic_network: Generated random graphs: Erdos-Renyi, Barabasi-Albert/scale-free, Watts-Strogatz/small-world, stochastic block, configuration models.
network_topology.adaptive_network: Topology coevolves with opinions: rewiring, link update or network adaptation driven by states.
network_topology.other_topology: Empirical/real networks, multilayer or multiplex networks, hypergraphs, temporal networks or other specified structures.

reported_outcomes.consensus: Convergence to agreement or a single opinion cluster.
reported_outcomes.persistent_diversity: Fragmentation, multiple clusters or coexistence reported without emphasis on polarization.
reported_outcomes.polarization: Bimodal or extreme opinion splits, polarization or echo chambers as outcomes.
reported_outcomes.other_outcome: Only explicitly reported outcomes outside consensus, persistent diversity and polarization: convergence time, cascade size, fit statistics, control or intervention effects.

study_design.analytical: Mathematical analysis: proofs, mean-field or exact solutions, stability analysis.
study_design.empirical: Analysis of empirical data or human experiments together with an opinion model.

validation_method.numerical: Numerical or simulation checks of model behaviour (sweeps, convergence, phase diagrams).
validation_method.empirical_macro: Comparison with aggregate empirical data: distributions, polls, election or platform-level statistics.
validation_method.empirical_micro: Comparison with individual-level data: panels, experiments, interaction traces.
validation_method.robustness: Sensitivity or robustness analyses across parameters, structures or assumptions.

empirical_grounding.observational_data: Observational empirical data: surveys, social media, voting or behavioural records.
empirical_grounding.other_data: Other data sources used to calibrate or test the model.
empirical_grounding.no_empirical_data_reported: The study is stated or evidently purely theoretical/computational with no empirical data.
empirical_grounding.not_reported: Cannot tell whether empirical data are used.

reproducibility_artifacts.environment: Code, software or model implementation availability stated.

evidence_gaps.macro_level_validation: Authors state a need for empirical or aggregate-level validation of opinion models.
evidence_gaps.model_comparison: Authors state a need to compare, discriminate or identify models or mechanisms.
evidence_gaps.other_author_stated_gap: Another gap or future direction explicitly stated by the authors.

development_note: Refined on the batch-0001 double-extraction sample (development); agreement is evaluated on a fresh random double-extraction sample from batch-0002.
